title: Robotics and Task Transfer
summary: How learned robotic behaviors transfer across tasks — reducing the data cost of each new task.
argument: Robotic systems trained on one task rarely transfer cleanly to the next. Grasping, navigating, and manipulating skills learned in one context don't generalize without starting nearly from scratch. This is a representation and generalization problem, not a compute problem.
This program studies what properties of a learned skill make it reusable, and how training regimes can produce transferable behaviors rather than task-specific solutions.
currentWork: Surveying transfer learning and meta-learning approaches in robotic manipulation and locomotion. Identifying experimental settings where transfer fails most predictably.
futureDirection: Developing low-data adaptation methods for manipulation tasks in unstructured environments.
